content:
Most app projects that fail do not fail in the code. They fail because nobody asked, early enough, whether the app solves a problem people will open their phone for. At TopWebExpert we build Android and iOS apps from our office on Sohna Road, Sector 49, and we spend the first conversation on that question before we talk about screens or budgets. This page explains how we approach mobile app development in Gurugram: what we build, how we decide on the technology, what a typical project looks like week by week, and when we tell a client not to build an app at all.

Start With the Job the App Has to Do

Every app we take on begins with a one-page statement of the job it does for a specific user. A delivery rider in Manesar needs to mark a drop-off with one thumb while standing next to a truck. A patient at a clinic on Golf Course Road needs to rebook an appointment without calling the front desk. A sales team in Udyog Vihar needs to log a site visit even when the basement parking has no signal. These are very different apps, and writing the job down first stops the project from turning into a list of features copied from a competitor.

From that statement we agree on the smallest version worth releasing. Anything outside it goes into a later-release list, not into the first build.

Native, Cross-Platform or a Web App: How We Choose

We do not have a favourite framework we push on every client. The choice follows from what the app needs:

  • Flutter or React Native for most business apps that need to run on both Android and iOS from one codebase. This usually keeps build and maintenance cost lower.
  • Native Kotlin (Android) or Swift (iOS) when the app leans heavily on device hardware, such as Bluetooth scanners, background location or camera processing.
  • A progressive web app (PWA) when users will only open it occasionally and would not bother installing anything. It works in the browser and can be added to the home screen.

The backend is typically Node.js or Laravel with a MySQL or PostgreSQL database, hosted on AWS or a similar cloud provider, with Firebase used for push notifications and crash reporting.

Details That Matter for Indian Users

An app that works well on a flagship phone in our office can struggle in the hands of real users. We design and test for the conditions most Indian users actually have:

  • Low-end Android phones with limited RAM and storage, so we keep the app size small and avoid heavy animations.
  • Patchy mobile data, so key screens cache content and forms save drafts offline.
  • Payments through UPI, cards and wallets via gateways such as Razorpay, with clear handling of failed and pending transactions.
  • WhatsApp Business API for order updates and OTPs, where customers are more likely to read a WhatsApp message than an email.
  • Hindi and Hinglish interface text when the audience needs it, planned from the start rather than bolted on later.
  • DPDP Act 2023 obligations: clear consent screens, collecting only the personal data you need, and a way for users to ask for deletion.

A Typical Build, Week by Week

Timelines depend on scope, but a first release of a business app usually follows this pattern:

  1. Weeks 1–2: Discovery. A workshop at our Sector 49 office or yours, user flows, a feature list split into "release 1" and "later", and a fixed quote.
  2. Weeks 3–4: Design. Wireframes, then clickable Figma screens you can try on your own phone before any code is written.
  3. Weeks 5–12: Development. Two-week sprints, each ending with a test build you install through TestFlight or an Android test link.
  4. Weeks 12–14: Testing and store submission. Device testing, fixes, store listings, privacy declarations and submission to Google Play and the App Store.
  5. After launch: a stabilisation period for bug fixes, then an optional maintenance plan covering OS updates and new features.

Simple apps can be quicker. Apps with complex integrations, such as an ERP connection or a multi-vendor marketplace, take longer, and we say so in the quote.

What We Need From You

  • One decision-maker who can approve screens within a few days.
  • Your brand assets, content and any existing API documentation.
  • Your own Google Play Console and Apple Developer accounts, so the app is listed under your business name.
  • Access to a few real users for feedback on the test builds.

Who Owns the App and the Code

Once the project is paid for, you own the source code, designs and store listings. The code lives in a Git repository under your account, the apps are published under your developer accounts, and server credentials are handed over at the end. If you later move to an in-house team or another vendor, nothing is locked up with us.

How We Check Quality

Every build is tested on a mix of devices, including budget Android phones, not just emulators. We run code reviews on every change, automated tests on business logic such as pricing and payments, and crash monitoring from day one of the beta. Before store submission we go through Google and Apple review guidelines to avoid rejections that delay launch.

Mistakes We Help Clients Avoid

  • Building every feature for version one instead of releasing a focused app and learning from usage.
  • Publishing under the agency's developer account, which makes switching vendors painful later.
  • Ignoring the admin panel. Your team will use it daily, so it needs as much care as the customer app.
  • Skipping a budget for maintenance. Android and iOS release updates every year, and apps need to keep up.

When an App Is the Wrong Answer

We are not a good fit if you want an app mainly because competitors have one, if customers interact with you once or twice a year, or if you need a working product in two weeks. In those cases a fast, mobile-friendly website or a WhatsApp-based flow is often the smarter spend, and we will tell you that in the first meeting.

Questions Gurugram Businesses Ask Us

How much does it cost to build an app?

Cost depends on the number of screens, the platforms, integrations such as payments or an ERP, and whether you need an admin panel. We do not quote from a rate card. After a free consultation and a short discovery, we give you a fixed quote tied to a written scope.

Can you take over an app another agency started?

Yes, provided we can get the source code and account access. We start with a code audit and tell you honestly whether to continue with the existing code or rebuild parts of it.

Will my app work on older Android phones?

We agree a minimum Android and iOS version at the start based on your users, and we test on lower-end devices before release.

Do we have to meet in person?

No, but many clients based in Cyber City, Golf Course Road or around Gurgaon's Sohna Road belt find a half-day workshop at our office the quickest way to settle scope. Everything after that can run on calls and shared test builds.

What happens after the app goes live?

We fix launch bugs as part of the project, then offer an optional monthly maintenance plan for OS updates, security patches and new features.
